inspection.spec: Measure ply_actual (default 0.75"). Keep inner span 16.5″.
P-001L/R identical hole pattern after stack-drill
Base diagonals equal; no rack
Both vertical ways plumb and coplanar in X; shoes wrap without bind through full travel
≤ 0.003″ on both diagonals of P-006
≤ 0.002″ mid-span

inspection.check: Drum ∥ table paper on (alias of QC-15)
inspection.spec: Use QC-15 ALN-01. |A−B| ≤ 0.003″ over 15.5″, no load.
Rollers 0.030″ below drum OD, paper on
Straightedge across both pulley faces
Use QC-16 TV-01. Witness-board spread ≤ 0.005″.
Shaft can grow axially; no banana preload
Shoes wrap tongue; project 0.230″; X play 0.010″; table moves in Z only
No rail in the table envelope; min Z gap 6.062″ (CALC-004)
Both screws at Y 11″; |left−right| travel match through 3″
Indicator at station A (drive) and B (idler), drum stopped, paper on, no workpiece: |A−B| ≤ 0.003″ over 15.5″. Set with the P-023 jack.
Witness board 15.5″ wide, finish pass: caliper 4 corners + centre, spread ≤ 0.005″. This is the user-facing number, NOT the same as QC-15.
Set gib to 0.0015″: table slides by hand through full travel with no perceptible rock at either end. Record the feeler used.
Knife-edge test: drum comes to rest in a random position over 5 releases. Allowance U ≤ 0.39 oz·in (CALC-C13).
Re-check all H-034 through-bolts after the first hour of running. Wood relaxes; a loose frame reads as taper.
Measured or vendor-curve airflow ≥ 349 CFM at the machine (CALC-C15). A shop vacuum will not meet this.

decisions.decision: Delete conveyor; solid sliding table
decisions.reason: Walters: conveyor is the failure point

decisions.decision: Keep 16.5″ inner span even if ply is 18 mm
decisions.reason: Capacity and drum length are the constraint, not outer width

decisions.decision: Dual ½-10 Acme + chain + left clutch/home dog
decisions.reason: One screw cannot hold coplanarity after paper wrap

decisions.decision: Fixed drive bearing, floating idler
decisions.reason: Two locked flanges banana the shaft

decisions.decision: UHMW let into a rebate; project only ~0.23″
decisions.reason: ¾″ proud ways steal 1.5″ and a 16″ table cannot enter a 16.5″ span

decisions.decision: ¼″ housed stretchers, not butt joints
decisions.reason: Racking stiffness without using stretchers as the table datum

decisions.decision: Persistent part IDs P/H/J/A; Python is SSOT
decisions.reason: Drawings, BOM, viewer, and OpenSCAD were duplicating 16.5 / 14 / 18.5

decisions.decision: Wandel-style individual part, assembly, and hardware sheets
decisions.reason: Overview D-sheets are not enough to fabricate P-001 from; each make part needs its own isometric + hole chart + callouts

decisions.decision: Idler float is an axial pad, not YZ slots in the side panel
decisions.reason: Face-plane slots let the drum axis wander; shaft growth is through the bearing

decisions.decision: Master build guide: release state on every sheet, ballooned explosion, numbered step sheets with parts trays
decisions.reason: A builder should follow numbered steps with per-step parts and QC gates, not reverse-engineer the order from overview sheets

decisions.decision: Vertical captured UHMW ways; table is a lifting carriage
decisions.reason: Horizontal ways at Z=10 never supported the table at operating height (11.5–15.9″). Capture in X/Y, Acme in Z.

decisions.decision: Three stretcher stations IN-LO / OUT-LO / OUT-HI, rails on edge
decisions.reason: A stretcher at Z=12 occupied the same volume as a 3″-open table. Triangle in the YZ plane fights racking without crossing the table.

decisions.decision: Both Acme screws on the drum centerline (left/right X, one Y)
decisions.reason: Infeed/outfeed Y put the nuts off the cutting-force line and the 3D model only drew two screws at one Y anyway. Force through the nuts; chain couples them.

decisions.decision: Layout protocol is HYBRID: face/edge on panels, centerline on drum/Acme/ways
decisions.reason: Planforge centerline protocol. Mixing a face measurement with a CL measurement without converting is how the drum axis drifts.

decisions.decision: Split the single 0.003 in spec into ALN-01 (no-load alignment) and TV-01 (delivered thickness variation, 0.005 in)
decisions.reason: Rev B quoted one number for two different measurable quantities. The error budgets differ by a factor of two and no machine can make them equal.

decisions.decision: Drum axis rebuilt: 1.25 in shaft, structural 5 in x 0.25 in 6061 shell, plugs 0.25 in inboard, bearings 0.35 in off the side face
decisions.reason: The 3/4 in shaft spent the whole accuracy allowance at 4.25 lbf. Rev C crowns 0.22 mil at 20 lbf, 21x stiffer.

decisions.decision: Adjustable tapered gib on the idler way replaces the 0.020 in sliding clearance; target 0.0015 in running clearance
decisions.reason: Way play was the largest single term in the Rev B thickness budget.

decisions.decision: Idler bearing on a pivot plate with a 1/4-28 jack screw, 6.00 in / 1.25 in arm reduction
decisions.reason: Parallelism must be settable finer than the spec. Resolution is 0.26 mil per 15 deg at the work.

decisions.decision: Lift screws carry the table in compression; always approach the setting from below and lock the ways before cutting
decisions.reason: Removes screw backlash from the budget without an anti-backlash nut. Screws are self-locking, so the table cannot drift down.

decisions.decision: Bearings specified by required dynamic capacity C, not by bore alone
decisions.reason: Rev B named a bearing by appearance. Rev C states the requirement so any vendor's data can be checked against it.

decisions.decision: Re-sheave to 3.5 in / 5 in -> 1208 rpm, 1581 sfpm
decisions.reason: Rev B ran 1355 sfpm, low for finish work. The option table lets the builder trade finish against unbalance sensitivity.

decisions.decision: Keep the MDF disc-stack drum as documented Option B
decisions.reason: A shop without lathe access cannot make the shell and plugs. Option B is honest about its accuracy penalty rather than hidden.

decisions.decision: Housed dado plus through-bolts with backing washers for the frame, not screws alone
decisions.reason: User standard: never rely on glue alone for primary structure, and a machine frame must be re-tightenable and knock-down.

Precision rebuild. Rev B's ¾″ shaft failed its own accuracy spec at 4.25 lbf (CALC-C01), and one 0.003″ figure was being used for two different quantities. Rev C: 1¼″ shaft + structural aluminium shell (21× stiffer), adjustable gib, parallelism micro-adjust plate, bearings specified by required dynamic capacity, spec split into ALN-01 and TV-01, frame through-bolted, 18-step build with an Option B drum, McMaster procurement register.

build_steps.title: Buy, acclimate, and measure the plywood
build_steps.goal: Know your real ply thickness before a single dado is cut.
actions: Stand the sheets on edge in the shop for at least 48 hours. Euro BB arrives at 18 mm, not ¾″.
Caliper the ply in six places. Record the number as ply_actual (model default 0.75″).
If it is not 0.75″, edit ply_actual in cad/walter_ds16.py and regenerate every sheet. Do not shave the 16.5″ inner span to make the old numbers work.
build_steps.gate: Measured ply thickness recorded. Inner span stays 16.5″ (419 mm).
build_steps.hold: Nothing is cut yet. This is the cheapest place to catch the 18 mm surprise.

build_steps.title: Rough-cut the panels oversize
build_steps.goal: Flat, labelled, manageable blanks out of full sheets.
actions: Cut every panel about ⅛″ over width and ¼″ over length. Final size comes off one stop later.
Write the part ID on each blank in pencil the moment it leaves the sheet.
Keep the two side blanks as a matched pair — they get drilled together in ST-04.
build_steps.gate: All blanks labelled, oversize, and stacked flat.
build_steps.warn: Full sheets are heavy and awkward. Support the offcut so it cannot drop onto the blade or onto you.

build_steps.title: Cut both sides to final size on one stop
build_steps.goal: Two panels that ARE the same size, not two panels that measure the same.
actions: Set the stop for 30″ and cut both panels (S-001). Do not move the stop between cuts.
Reset for 22″ depth and cut both (S-002).
Mark the INNER face and the INFEED edge on each panel. Those two marks are Datum C and Datum B for the rest of the build.
build_steps.gate: Panels identical within a pencil line; inner face and infeed edge marked on both.
build_steps.correctable: Nothing about panel size after this — the drum and table depend on it.

build_steps.title: Stack-drill the pair: bearing, flange, pilots
build_steps.goal: One hole pattern, drilled once, so the drum axis cannot be crooked.
actions: Clamp the panels face-to-face, inner faces together, infeed edges flush.
Lay out the bearing centreline at Y 11″ from the infeed edge and Z 18.5″ up from the bottom.
Set the actual flange on the panel and transfer its bolt holes. The drawing shows 3″ square as a placeholder — your bearing decides.
Drill the ⌀1.625″ shaft clearance and the four bolt holes through both panels at once (S-008).
Drive side only: pilot the motor pivot at Y 4″ / Z 6″ and the indicator pad at Y 8″ / Z 16″.
build_steps.gate: Panels separated; hole patterns line up when the panels are flipped face-to-face.
build_steps.hold: Stop here until the flange is in your hand. Do not drill this pattern from the drawing alone.
build_steps.warn: Clamp hard. A panel that shifts mid-drill gives you two different machines.
build_steps.correctable: Almost nothing. This pattern is the datum for the whole machine.

build_steps.title: Dado the stretcher housings and way rebates
build_steps.goal: Inner-face joinery, mirrored — the one operation where the panels are NOT identical.
tools: Dado stack or router + edge guide
actions: Split the pair. From here the panels are mirror images — work only on the marked inner faces.
Cut three stretcher housings 0.25″ deep × 0.75″ wide × 4″ tall at stations IN-LO, OUT-LO, OUT-HI (J-001, S-006). Rails stand on edge. None of these dados may sit at Z ≈ 12 — that is the table.
Rout the vertical way rebate 0.520″ deep × 2.5″ wide, Y 9.75–12.25″ (drum CL), Z 11–16.438″ (J-002, S-007).
Test the dado width on an offcut of the same ply first. A sloppy housing is a racking frame.
build_steps.gate: Rebate 0.520″ deep ±0.010″; a scrap of way stock sits 0.230″ proud. Dados at IN-LO / OUT-LO / OUT-HI only.
build_steps.warn: Do not dado the panels while they are still stacked. You will get two left-hand sides.
build_steps.correctable: A rebate can go deeper, never shallower.

build_steps.title: Glue the box: stretchers, base, diagonals
build_steps.goal: A square, stiff carcase that will not rack when a board is pushed through it.
actions: Dry-fit all three stretchers (17″, housed 0.25″ each end) into IN-LO, OUT-LO, OUT-HI. Check the inner span reads 16.5″. Confirm no rail sits in the table's Z range (11.5–15.94″).
Glue and clamp. Measure both diagonals and pull them equal before the glue grabs.
With the joint clamped, drill through the side into each stretcher end and fit H-034 ¼-20 through-bolts with backing washers and nylocks (D-048). Glue is not primary structure on this machine.
Screw the base deck on, then measure the diagonals again.
build_steps.gate: Diagonals equal within 1/32″. Inner span 16.5″ at top, middle, and bottom.
build_steps.hold: Let the glue cure before hanging anything heavy on the box.

build_steps.title: Bond the vertical UHMW ways and wax them
build_steps.goal: Two plumb rails for the table shoes to wrap. These, not the stretchers, locate the table in X and Y.
actions: Cut two UHMW strips 5.438″ × 2.5″ and set them into the vertical rebates. They should project 0.230″.
Bond and clamp. Optional: #8 flush screws from the outer face.
Square both ways to the base. An indicator riding a tall square should read the same on left and right.
Paste wax only. Never oil — oil migrates into the wood and into your finish.
build_steps.gate: Ways plumb. Projection 0.230″ ±0.010″. Centered on drum CL at Y 11″.
build_steps.correctable: UHMW can be planed down; it cannot be built back up.

build_steps.title: Make the tapered gib and tap the adjuster stations
build_steps.goal: Have the gib ready before the table exists. Running clearance is set later, after the shoes are on.
actions: Taper one face of P-022 at 1:40 over its 22″ length. Mark the thick end so it cannot go in backwards.
Drill and tap three ¼-20 stations in the idler-side panel for the H-031 brass-tip adjusters (S-013).
Dry-fit the gib in the rebate behind where the idler shoe will sit. Taper wedges DOWN: tightening a screw will close the clearance.
Do not set the running clearance yet — there is no table to rock against. That happens in the table chapter after the shoes are on.
build_steps.gate: Gib tapered, thick end marked, three adjuster stations tapped, dry-fit confirmed.
build_steps.warn: A gib installed thick-end-up opens when you tighten. Mark the thick end before it leaves the taper jig.
build_steps.correctable: Taper and length — the gib is still a loose part.

build_steps.title: Turn the two end plugs — one setup, two operations
build_steps.goal: Bore and OD concentric, because that error becomes drum TIR directly.
actions: Face and turn the OD to a light bond fit in the shell ID (4.5″ nominal — measure YOUR tube).
WITHOUT unchucking, bore 1.25″ for the shaft. One setup is the whole trick: it makes bore and OD concentric.
Part off at 1.5″ thick. Repeat for the second plug.
Deburr both, then check the bore on the actual shaft — light push fit, no rock.
build_steps.gate: Bore-to-OD runout under 0.001″ on each plug, checked in the lathe before parting off.
build_steps.warn: If you re-chuck between the OD and the bore you will add eccentricity that no amount of truing removes, because the drum will run true only at one angular position.
build_steps.correctable: Nothing after parting off. Make a spare plug from the same bar.

build_steps.title: Bond and cross-pin the shell to the plugs
build_steps.goal: A structural drum, not a stack of discs.
actions: Cut the shell to 15.75″ and face both ends square.
Abrade and solvent-clean the shell ID and both plug ODs. Contamination is the usual cause of a failed metal bond.
Mix H-033 structural epoxy, coat both faces, and seat each plug 0.25″ inboard of the shell end. Check square to the shell axis.
After cure, cross-drill and pin each plug through the shell wall in two places 90° apart. The pins carry torque; the epoxy seals and shares load.
build_steps.gate: Both plugs seated at the specified inset, square, fully cured, and pinned.
build_steps.hold: FULL CURE per the adhesive data sheet before the drum turns under power. This is a 18 lb rotating assembly.
build_steps.warn: Never rely on adhesive alone on a rotating part. The cross-pins are not optional.
build_steps.correctable: The OD — that is what truing is for. Not the plug position.

build_steps.title: OPTION B — laminated disc drum for a shop with no lathe
build_steps.goal: A buildable drum without turned metal, with its accuracy penalty stated.
actions: Choose this path ONLY if you cannot get the plugs turned. It replaces steps ST-09 and ST-10.
Bandsaw 19 MDF discs and 2 birch ends at ⌀5.125″ — oversize on purpose.
Stack the whole pack in the P-015 jig and ream ⌀1.25″ straight through (J-005, S-009). Never bore discs one at a time.
Glue the stack with a 1 mm relief every 4 MDF discs. Birch ends outboard for flange crush.
Weigh the two end discs against each other and balance them before assembly.
build_steps.gate: Bore accepts the shaft with light friction. Stack length 15.75″.
build_steps.hold: Full cure before the drum ever spins. A delaminated disc at speed is a projectile.
build_steps.warn: ACCEPT THE PENALTY KNOWINGLY: a disc stack is not structural in bending, so the drum crowns under load and MDF moves with humidity, so TIR drifts between seasons. Expect to re-true more often and to hold a looser TV-01 than 0.005″.
build_steps.correctable: Outside diameter — that is what truing is for.

build_steps.title: Hang the shaft: drive FIXED, idler on the micro-adjust plate
build_steps.goal: One bearing defines the axis; the other adjusts parallelism and lets the shaft grow.
actions: Transfer the bearing bolt pattern FROM THE BEARING YOU BOUGHT onto P-001L and P-023. Do not drill from the drawing — that pattern is an assumption.
Slide the 24″ shaft through the drum and both panels, then set the H-029 clamp collars against the plugs.
Bolt H-001 to the drive side and torque it. That bearing is now DATUM-E, the drum-axis datum (J-006).
Pin P-023 to the idler side with H-032, mount H-002 on it, and set the H-030 jack screw against P-024. Snug the bearing only — the shaft must still slide axially (J-007).
Spin the drum by hand through several turns. It should coast, not bind and not ring.
build_steps.gate: Shaft turns freely; measurable axial float at the idler end; jack screw makes contact with a witness mark.
build_steps.warn: Locking both bearings bends the shaft and kills both of them. Do not do it because it feels tighter.
build_steps.correctable: Bearing position, while the bolts are still loose.

build_steps.title: True the drum in its own bearings, then balance it
build_steps.goal: A cylinder that is round about the axis it will actually run on.
tools: Knife edges or two level rails
actions: True the OD with the drum running in its OWN bearings, using the full-width P-013 sled. Truing it in a lathe and then moving it re-introduces the error.
Work down until the indicator reads ≤ 0.0015″ TIR at mid-span, paper off (QC-06).
Lift the drum onto knife edges and release it from five different angular positions. It must stop somewhere different each time. Allowance U ≤ 0.39 oz·in (CALC-C13).
If it always settles the same way, add tape to the light side until it does not, then make that correction permanent.
build_steps.gate: TIR ≤ 0.0015″ paper off, and the knife-edge test passes over five releases.
build_steps.hold: Do not fit the abrasive until both checks pass. Paper hides TIR; it does not fix it.
build_steps.warn: Extraction and a respirator for truing. Eye protection — you are cutting metal or MDF at speed.
build_steps.correctable: Balance, any time. TIR only by truing again.

build_steps.title: Mount the motor, align the pulleys, lock the cradle
build_steps.goal: Belt tension by gravity, then locked so it cannot pump.
actions: Pivot P-012 on the drive-side hole and hang the 1 HP motor on it.
Fit the 3.5″ motor pulley and the 5″ drum pulley. Lay a straightedge across both faces and shim until they are coplanar.
Let the cradle hang to tension the belt, measure the centre distance, then buy the belt to that number.
Lock the cradle. A cradle that still swings will pump the belt and chirp.
build_steps.gate: Pulley faces coplanar; belt tracks centred when the drum is turned by hand.
build_steps.warn: Mains wiring, switch, and grounding belong to a qualified electrician and your local code. This package does not release electrical work.
build_steps.correctable: Belt length, before you buy it.

build_steps.title: Build the torsion-box table and bond the wear face
build_steps.goal: A flat plate that stays flat. This is the surface you measure against forever.
actions: Glue the rib grid at 4″ o.c. between the two skins. Full glue, clamped on a flat reference.
Check the box flat in both directions and on both diagonals. Flatten it before going further.
Bond the phenolic or tooling-plate wear face on top (J-004).
Groove and bolt P-017 shoes under each long edge, centered on Y 11″. Groove 0.240″ × 2.516″ wraps the way tongue (J-012).
Confirm the finished plan size is 16″ × 22″ so the wear face still carries 15.5″ of work.
build_steps.gate: Wear face flat within 0.003″ on both diagonals.
build_steps.hold: Cure fully. Every later measurement trusts this plane.
build_steps.correctable: Flatness, while the box is still open.

build_steps.title: Fit the dual Acme lift on the drum centerline
build_steps.goal: Both nuts sit under the cut. The table rises in Z without racking in X or Y.
actions: Screw both P-018 thrust blocks to the base at Y 11″ (drum CL), X left and right. Fit thrust washers and e-clips (J-013).
Bolt a bronze nut block under the table, each nut on the same Y as its screw — not at the infeed and outfeed ends.
Fit both ½-10 Acme screws. One turn is 0.1000″. Thirty turns is 3″ (CALC-003).
Chain-couple the two screws. Fit the left clutch and P-019 home dog (J-014).
Run the table through the full 3.25″ of travel. Shoes must stay wrapped; the table must not yaw.

Now set the P-022 gib: slide it behind the idler shoe, taper down, and run the H-031 adjusters up in equal steps until the table slides by hand with no rock. Target 0.0015″ (QC-17, S-014). Wax. Never oil.
build_steps.gate: Table rises and falls freely through full travel; both ends move the same amount; shoes stay captured; gib clearance 0.0015″ with no rock.
build_steps.correctable: Nut block position, before the holes are final.

build_steps.title: Kerf-bend the hood and set the roller yokes
build_steps.goal: The guard that is also the dust hood, plus the rollers that kill snipe.
actions: Kerf-bend the hood blank around the drum arc, glue the form, fill the kerfs, and fit the 4″ port.
Hang both roller yokes on shoulder-bolt pivots with light compression springs.
Set each roller 0.030″ below the drum OD with paper on, using feeler gauges.
Check the hood clears the drum, the rollers, and the oscillator stroke if you fitted one.
build_steps.gate: Both rollers 0.030″ below drum OD, paper on. Hood seats without touching the drum.
build_steps.warn: Hood ON is the primary guard. Open it only with the machine stopped and unplugged.
build_steps.correctable: Spring rate and roller height, any time.

build_steps.title: True, wrap, re-clock, and cut a witness board
build_steps.goal: Turn an assembled machine into a calibrated one.
actions: Paper off: true the drum with the full-width sled until TIR ≤ 0.002″ mid-span (S-010).
Wrap Velcro, then spiral the paper. Paper thickness is not uniform, so parallel changes here.

ALN-01: paper on, drum stopped, no workpiece. Indicate the drum at station A (drive) and station B (idler). Bring |A−B| ≤ 0.003″ using the P-023 jack screw — 6.17 mil at the work per full turn, so work in small fractions of a turn. Set the home dog (S-011).
TV-01: sand a witness board 15.5″ wide at the finish pass. Caliper four corners and the centre. Spread must be ≤ 0.005″. This is a different and larger number than ALN-01 — see CALC-C06.
Then work the pass schedule: 0.008″ rough, 0.004″ medium, 0.001″ finish. Always approach the setting by RAISING the table, then lock the ways.
build_steps.gate: TIR ≤ 0.0015″ paper-off · ALN-01 |A−B| ≤ 0.003″ paper-on · TV-01 witness spread ≤ 0.005″.
build_steps.hold: First powered run: hood on, no stock, stand clear of the drum ends, hand on the switch.
build_steps.warn: Do not sand stock shorter than about 12″ without the sled. Hands never under the drum or the hold-downs.
build_steps.correctable: Everything that matters — which is why you re-clock after every paper change.

calculations.name: Stretcher vs table envelope
calculations.expr: min Z gap, all three rails, table at every opening

calculations.name: Drum rotational energy
calculations.expr: ½ I ω² · m≈10.1 lb · 1207.5 RPM

calculations.name: Does the Rev B 3/4 in shaft hold the accuracy spec?
calculations.method: Simply supported beam, load patch over drum, numeric M/EI

calculations.name: Rev C load-induced drum crown
calculations.method: Series model: shell plug-to-plug, then shaft bearing-to-bearing

calculations.name: What sanding force may the drum axis carry?
calculations.method: Linear scaling of CALC-C02 to the allowance

calculations.name: Alignment budget, no load (ALN)
calculations.inputs: Drum TIR, paper-on 1.50 mil; Micro-adjust setting resolution at work 0.26 mil; Indicator + stand repeatability 0.50 mil; Drum straightness over 15.5 in 0.50 mil
calculations.method: Worst-case sum and RSS of setup terms

calculations.name: Delivered thickness variation, Rev B vs Rev C (TV)
calculations.result: Rev B RSS 21.8 mil -> Rev C RSS 4.5 mil
calculations.method: Error budget under cut load across 15.5 in

calculations.name: Is 0.003 in a legitimate single specification?
calculations.result: Two different quantities; TV cannot equal ALN
calculations.verdict: Rev B spec DEFECT — split into ALN-01 and TV-01
calculations.inputs: ALN RSS 1.68 mil vs TV RSS 4.51 mil
calculations.method: Compare the two budgets that Rev B collapsed into one number

calculations.name: Parallelism micro-adjust resolution
calculations.expr: rise = lead x L2/L1; at work x capacity/span
calculations.result: 6.17 mil/rev at the work; 0.257 mil per 15 deg
calculations.method: Fine-thread jack on a pivot plate, reduction L2/L1

calculations.name: Required bearing self-aligning capability
calculations.criterion: within the insert's static misalignment rating
calculations.method: Angle subtended by the alignment spec

calculations.name: Lift screw torque and back-drive behaviour
calculations.expr: T = F dm/2 (L + pi mu dm sec a)/(pi dm - mu L sec a)
calculations.inputs: dm=0.450 in, lead=0.100 in, mu=0.15 [A], load 23.4 lbf/screw

calculations.name: Lift resolution at the handwheel
calculations.criterion: <= finish pass 1 mil is not required; must be readable
calculations.margin: one division is a legible finish increment

calculations.name: Required bearing dynamic capacity
calculations.margin: specify by requirement, not by appearance
calculations.method: ISO-form L10 life inverted for C

calculations.name: Drum speed and surface speed at the selected sheaves
calculations.expr: n = n_m d_m/d_d ; sfpm = pi D n / 12
calculations.verdict: PASS — see M-102 for the full option table

calculations.name: Allowable residual drum unbalance
calculations.criterion: 1 lbf rotating force at the bearings
calculations.margin: ~4.4 g of tape at r=2.5 in is the whole allowance

calculations.name: First bending critical speed
calculations.method: Uniform simply supported beam, shaft EI with full drum mass

calculations.name: Dust extraction requirement
calculations.criterion: collector must deliver this AT THE MACHINE
calculations.margin: a shop vac will not do this
calculations.method: Duct area x transport velocity; hood face velocity

calculations.name: Way bearing stress on the UHMW
calculations.verdict: PASS — the way is precision-limited, not stress-limited

calculations.name: Tipping stability against feed force
calculations.result: 77 lbf to tip vs 8 lbf feed
calculations.verdict: PASS — still bolt or cleat the stand
calculations.method: Restoring vs overturning moment about the base edge

calculations.name: Solo handling of every module
calculations.result: Side 12 lb; Base 7 lb; Table 19 lb; Drum 18 lb; Frame 38 lb
calculations.margin: assembled machine must be built in place
calculations.verdict: PASS per module; assembled total exceeds the limit by design
calculations.method: Volume x density per module vs lift limit

procurement.description: Aluminum round tube, 5" OD x 0.25" wall — drum shell
procurement.controlling_spec: 6061-T6, 5" OD, 0.25" wall (ID 4.5"). Wall is a stiffness requirement, not cosmetic: I = 10.55 in^4.
procurement.hole_or_prep: Cut 1/8 long, face both ends square in a lathe or on a sled. Bore/turn OD true AFTER assembly to the shaft.
procurement.installation: Bond + pin to P-021 plugs. See J-106.
procurement.substitution_rule: Any 6061 or 6063 tube with OD 5.000 -0.000/+0.030 and wall >= 0.180 in. Do NOT substitute thin-wall decorative tube: wall drives the stiffness in CALC-C02.
procurement.search_query: 6061 aluminum round tube 5" OD 0.25" wall

procurement.description: Precision-ground rotary shaft, 1.25" dia — drum shaft
procurement.controlling_spec: 1.25" dia, ground and polished, straightness <= 0.001"/ft, surface finish suitable for a set-screw insert.
procurement.mating_parts: P-010 shaft, H-001/H-002 bearings, P-021 plugs, H-004 sheave
procurement.hole_or_prep: Cut to length, chamfer both ends 0.030 x 45 deg, deburr. Do not centre-punch the bearing seats.
procurement.installation: Slide through the drum and both panels together — see ST-12.
procurement.substitution_rule: 1045 TG&P or 1566 ground shafting, 1.25" -0.001/-0.000. Hot-rolled bar is NOT acceptable: TIR would consume the whole alignment budget.
procurement.search_query: precision ground rotary shaft 1.25 inch diameter

procurement.description: Mounted ball bearing, 1.25" bore, self-aligning insert
procurement.controlling_spec: 1.25" bore, spherical-seat (self-aligning) insert, set-screw or eccentric-collar locking, sealed. REQUIRED basic dynamic capacity C >= 137 lbf for 5000 h at 1208 rpm. Static misalignment capability >= 0.011 deg.
procurement.mating_parts: P-001L (fixed), P-023 idler adjust plate (floating), P-010 shaft
procurement.hole_or_prep: Bolt pattern: MEASURE the flange you receive and transfer to P-001L / P-023. Do not drill from the drawing — flange bolt circle is [A].
procurement.installation: Drive end LOCKED. Idler end axially FREE. Never lock both — see J-007.
procurement.substitution_rule: Any 2- or 4-bolt flange or pillow block meeting the bore, the C requirement and the self-aligning requirement. Confirm C on the vendor page; a bearing chosen by bore alone is not specified.
procurement.search_query: mounted ball bearing flange 1.25 inch bore self-aligning

procurement.description: Aluminum round bar, 4-1/2" dia — drum end plugs
procurement.controlling_spec: 6061-T6 round bar, >= 4.5" dia. Turn to a light press/bond fit in the shell ID and bore 1.25" H7-equivalent for the shaft.
procurement.mating_parts: P-021 plug, P-020 shell, P-010 shaft
procurement.hole_or_prep: Bore 1.25" on the same setup as the OD turn so bore and OD are concentric. Concentricity here becomes drum TIR.
procurement.installation: Bond into shell, cross-pin, then clamp to shaft — see J-106.
procurement.substitution_rule: Phenolic or hard maple acceptable for Option B only; aluminum preferred because it holds the bore under humidity change.
procurement.search_query: 6061 aluminum round bar 4-1/2 inch diameter

procurement.controlling_spec: Two-piece or single-piece clamping collar, 1.25" bore, steel or aluminum. Used to locate the plugs axially and to set the fixed-bearing shoulder. Clamp type only — set-screw collars mar the ground shaft.
procurement.mating_parts: P-010 shaft, P-021 plugs, H-001 bearing
procurement.hole_or_prep: None. Do not drill the shaft.
procurement.installation: Tighten opposite-corner sequence to the collar maker's torque.
procurement.substitution_rule: Any clamp-style collar of the correct bore. Set-screw collars are excluded by interface, not by preference.
procurement.search_query: clamping shaft collar 1.25 inch bore two piece

procurement.description: Socket head cap screw, 1/4-28 — parallelism micro-adjust jack
procurement.controlling_spec: 1/4-28 x 1-1/2" alloy socket head cap screw. Fine thread is the requirement: lead 0.03571" gives 0.26 mil at the work per 15 deg of knob.
procurement.mating_parts: P-023 idler adjust plate, P-024 jack block
procurement.hole_or_prep: Tap P-024 1/4-28 through. Chase the thread clean; a ragged thread shows up as backlash in the adjustment.
procurement.installation: Brass or nylon tip pad under the screw point so it does not dig into the plate and lose calibration.
procurement.substitution_rule: M6x0.75 acceptable if the lead is recomputed and the sheet is revised. Do NOT use 1/4-20: resolution degrades ~40%.
procurement.search_query: 1/4-28 socket head cap screw alloy steel 1-1/2 long

procurement.controlling_spec: 1/4-20 brass-tipped or nylon-tipped set screw. Brass tip loads the gib without embedding in it.
procurement.hole_or_prep: Tap 3 stations per way, 1/4-20.
procurement.installation: Set gib for 1.5 mil running clearance: table slides by hand with no perceptible rock. Q-102 records it.
procurement.substitution_rule: Any tipped set screw. A bare steel set screw is excluded: it brinells the gib and the setting drifts.
procurement.search_query: brass tipped set screw 1/4-20

procurement.description: Hardened dowel pin, 3/8" x 2" — idler plate pivot
procurement.controlling_spec: 3/8" x 2" hardened, ground dowel pin. The pivot must not wear oval or the parallelism setting walks.
procurement.mating_parts: P-023 idler adjust plate, P-001R side
procurement.hole_or_prep: Ream 3/8" for a light press in the plate, slip fit in the side.
procurement.installation: Press into the plate, retain with a collar or E-clip.
procurement.substitution_rule: Ground shoulder bolt of the same diameter is acceptable.
procurement.search_query: hardened precision dowel pin 3/8 x 2

procurement.description: Dial indicator, 1" travel, 0.001" graduations + magnetic base
procurement.controlling_spec: Travel >= 1", resolution 0.001", lug or stem back. Magnetic base with a fine adjust. This is the instrument that proves ALN-01 and TV-01.
procurement.mating_parts: Q-101 acceptance, indicator pad on P-001L
procurement.hole_or_prep: 1/4-20 tapped pad already on P-001L.
procurement.installation: Read at station A (drive) and station B (idler), paper on, spindle perpendicular to the table.
procurement.substitution_rule: 0.0005" indicator or a digital caliper in wooden blocks. A tape measure cannot verify this specification.
procurement.search_query: dial indicator 1 inch travel 0.001 graduation magnetic base

procurement.controlling_spec: 1/2-10 single-lead Acme, steel. Lead 0.100"/rev gives 2.50 mil per handwheel division.
procurement.mating_parts: P-016 nut block, P-018 thrust block, H-008 chain
procurement.hole_or_prep: Cut square, chase the end thread, chamfer.
procurement.installation: Loaded in COMPRESSION under the table. Always approach the final setting by raising — see D-034.
procurement.substitution_rule: 1/2-10 2-start acme is NOT interchangeable: it doubles the lead and halves the resolution. Revise the sheet if used.
procurement.search_query: 1/2-10 acme threaded rod lead screw

procurement.controlling_spec: Bronze or acetal Acme nut to match MC-10 lead. Flanged preferred so it can be bolted to P-016.
procurement.hole_or_prep: Bore P-016 for a press fit; do not rely on adhesive alone.
procurement.installation: Both nuts installed before the chain is fitted so the table cannot cock.
procurement.substitution_rule: Any nut matching the screw lead and axial load. Verify the thread is the same hand and lead as MC-10.
procurement.search_query: bronze acme nut 1/2-10

procurement.qty: 1 x 3 ft chain, 2 sprockets, 1 connecting link
procurement.controlling_spec: #25 roller chain, two matched sprockets 1/2" bore with set screw. Equal tooth count is mandatory — unequal sprockets tilt the table.
procurement.hole_or_prep: Key or set-screw flat on each screw end.
procurement.installation: Fit with both screws at the SAME height, verified by indicator before the chain is closed.
procurement.substitution_rule: Timing belt and matched pulleys are acceptable and quieter. Tooth counts must be equal.
procurement.search_query: roller chain 25 sprocket 1/2 inch bore

procurement.controlling_spec: Handwheel >= 4" dia, 1/2" bore, with a graduated or markable rim. 40 divisions -> 2.50 mil per division.
procurement.hole_or_prep: Set screw flat on the screw end.
procurement.installation: Index the dial to zero at the home dog (P-019).
procurement.substitution_rule: Plain handwheel plus a shop-made paper dial is acceptable if graduation count is recorded on Q-102.
procurement.search_query: handwheel graduated dial 1/2 inch bore 4 inch

procurement.description: UHMW bar, 3/4" x 2-1/2" — vertical ways and gib
procurement.controlling_spec: UHMW-PE bar 3/4" x 2-1/2". Two ways plus gib stock plus spare. Dry bearing: wax only, never oil.
procurement.hole_or_prep: Machine the gib taper 1:40 on the table saw with a taper jig.
procurement.installation: Way stress is only 2.3 psi, so the way is precision-limited, not load-limited. Set the fit, not the tightness.
procurement.substitution_rule: Acetal or cast nylon acceptable; both move more with humidity than UHMW. PTFE is too soft for the gib.
procurement.search_query: UHMW polyethylene bar 3/4 x 2-1/2

procurement.description: Canvas or linen phenolic sheet, 1/2" — table wear face
procurement.controlling_spec: 1/2" canvas-base phenolic. This is DATUM-D, the metrology surface. Flatness after bonding must be <= 3 mil over the 15.5" contact line.
procurement.hole_or_prep: Scuff the bond face; keep the show face clean of adhesive.
procurement.installation: Bond to a FLATTENED torsion box. Check with a straightedge and feelers before it cures — Q-101.
procurement.substitution_rule: 3/8" MIC-6 cast aluminum plate is a better metrology surface and an acceptable substitute. Ordinary rolled plate is not: it is not flat enough.
procurement.search_query: canvas phenolic sheet 1/2 inch thick

procurement.controlling_spec: 5" pitch dia, A/4L section, 1.25" bore, keyed or set-screw. With the 3.5" motor sheave this gives 1208 rpm.
procurement.hole_or_prep: None; do not drill the ground shaft.
procurement.installation: Coplanar with the motor sheave — straightedge across both faces, QC-09.
procurement.substitution_rule: Any A/4L sheave of the same pitch diameter and bore. Changing diameter changes surface speed — recompute CALC-C12.
procurement.search_query: v-belt pulley 5 inch 1.25 inch bore A section

procurement.controlling_spec: 3.5" pitch dia, A/4L section, bore to match the motor shaft (MEASURE it — 5/8" is common but not universal).
procurement.hole_or_prep: Measure the motor shaft before ordering. [M] required.
procurement.installation: Set flush and coplanar; lock the set screw on the shaft flat.
procurement.substitution_rule: Match pitch diameter and the measured motor bore.
procurement.search_query: v-belt pulley 3.5 inch A section 5/8 bore

procurement.qty: 1 ea (size after the cradle is locked)
procurement.controlling_spec: A/4L section. Length is measured, not predicted: lock the motor cradle, then measure the centre distance and compute pitch length.
procurement.hole_or_prep: None.
procurement.installation: Tension by cradle weight, then lock so the belt cannot pump.
procurement.substitution_rule: Link belt is an acceptable and quieter substitute.
procurement.search_query: 4L v-belt

procurement.controlling_spec: Light compression spring, ~3/4" OD, free length ~2". Light is the requirement: a stiff spring bows thin stock and you sand a banana.
procurement.hole_or_prep: Spring pockets bored in P-014.
procurement.installation: Set rollers 30 mil below drum OD, paper on — QC-08.
procurement.substitution_rule: Any spring that lets a 1/16" board pass without visible bow.
procurement.search_query: compression spring 3/4 od 2 inch free length light

procurement.controlling_spec: 5/16" shoulder screw x 1-1/2". Shoulder gives a true pivot; a threaded bolt in a wood bearing wallows.
procurement.hole_or_prep: Ream the pivot for the shoulder, tap for the thread.
procurement.installation: Snug, then back off 1/8 turn so the yoke swings free.
procurement.substitution_rule: Ground dowel plus retaining collar.
procurement.search_query: shoulder screw 5/16 x 1-1/2

procurement.description: 4" dust hose, cuff and blast gate
procurement.controlling_spec: 4" ID flex hose, one cuff, one blast gate. The collector must deliver 349 CFM AT THE MACHINE — hood face velocity 609 fpm.
procurement.hole_or_prep: 4" port let into the hood.
procurement.installation: Shortest possible run, minimum elbows.
procurement.substitution_rule: Any 4" fitting. A shop vacuum will NOT meet the CFM requirement and will clog — this is a capacity requirement, not a connector preference.
procurement.search_query: 4 inch dust collection hose blast gate cuff

procurement.controlling_spec: Two-part structural epoxy rated for metal-to-metal bonding, with a published open time long enough to seat the plugs.
procurement.hole_or_prep: Abrade and solvent-clean both bond faces. Bond area and cure per the maker's data sheet — read it, do not assume.
procurement.installation: Cross-pin the joint as well: the pins carry torque, the epoxy seals and shares load. Never adhesive alone on a rotating part.
procurement.substitution_rule: Any structural metal-bonding epoxy with published shear strength and cure schedule. Do not use general-purpose 5-minute epoxy.
procurement.design_basis: J-106; user standard: never glue alone for primary structure
procurement.search_query: two part structural epoxy adhesive metal bonding

procurement.controlling_spec: 4" hook strip with pressure-sensitive adhesive; 3" loop-backed abrasive. Abrasive thickness variation is 2 mil of the TV-01 budget — buy one brand and stay with it.
procurement.hole_or_prep: Degrease the shell OD before applying PSA.
procurement.installation: Spiral wrap, no overlap, no gap. Re-clock ALN-01 after every grit change.
procurement.substitution_rule: Any loop-backed abrasive of consistent thickness.
procurement.search_query: hook and loop sanding drum wrap abrasive roll 3 inch

procurement.description: Hex bolts, nylock nuts and backing washers — frame through-bolts
procurement.controlling_spec: 1/4-20 hex bolt with a large-OD backing washer under both head and nut. Through-bolted frame is re-tightenable and knock-down.
procurement.hole_or_prep: Clamp the joint, then drill through both parts so the holes cannot disagree.
procurement.installation: Snug in an opposite-corner pattern, check diagonals, then final tighten. Re-check after the first hour of running — QC-13.
procurement.substitution_rule: 3/8" bolts acceptable; screws alone are excluded by the user joinery standard.
procurement.search_query: 1/4-20 hex bolt 3 inch nylock nut fender washer

procurement.controlling_spec: 3/8-16 male adjustable handle or star knob. Way locks and yoke locks.
procurement.hole_or_prep: Tapped inserts or T-nuts.
procurement.installation: Lock the ways BEFORE cutting — this removes the last of the lift compliance.
procurement.substitution_rule: Any 3/8-16 knob with a comfortable grip.
procurement.search_query: adjustable handle 3/8-16 star knob

layout_protocol.face_edge: DATUM-A bottom edge, DATUM-B infeed edge, DATUM-C inner face. Panel size, dado locations, and screw pilots originate here.
layout_protocol.centerline: Drum axis (DATUM-E), both Acme screws, vertical ways, and the table midplane all share Y = side_depth/2 from DATUM-B. Vertical locations originate from DATUM-A.
layout_protocol.declaration: Primary layout system: HYBRID. Panel joinery is face/edge. Drum, lift, and ways are centerline from DATUM-B / DATUM-A.

assembly.title: Template & stack-drill sides
assembly.body: Clamp P-001L/R face-to-face. Drill bearing CL at Y 11″ / Z 18.5″, Acme holes, indicator pad as one stack (S-008).

assembly.title: Dados, vertical way rebates, box + UHMW
assembly.body: Split the pair. Dado J-001 stations IN-LO/OUT-LO/OUT-HI and rebate vertical J-002 (0.520″) on inner faces only. Glue P-003, square diagonals, bond P-007.

assembly.title: Option A shell (baseline) or Option B discs
assembly.body: Option A: turn P-021 plugs in one setup, bond+pin into P-020 (J-106). Option B: bandsaw P-008/P-009, pack-bore ⌀1.25″ in P-015 (J-005). True in the machine's own bearings.

assembly.title: Fixed drive bearing, floating idler on micro-adjust plate
assembly.body: H-001 locked on P-001L (J-006). H-002 on P-023 jack plate (J-105 / J-007). Transfer the purchased flange BCD. Do not lock both bearings.

assembly.title: Motor cradle, coplanar pulleys, lock
assembly.body: Straightedge across H-003/H-004. Gravity tension, lock P-012 (J-008).

assembly.title: Torsion-box table + wear face + shoes
assembly.body: P-004 + P-005 @ 4″ o.c., glue. Flatten. Bond P-006. Fit P-017 shoes. Diagonals ≤ 0.003″.

assembly.title: Dual Acme lift on drum CL + chain couple
assembly.body: P-018 thrust on base, P-016 nuts, both screws at drum CL Y. H-008 chain. Left clutch + P-019 home dog. Table rises in Z; shoes stay wrapped.

assembly.title: Hold-down roller yokes
assembly.body: P-014 + H-009. Set 0.030″ below drum OD, paper on. Too much spring = snipe.

assembly.title: Kerf-bend dust hood
assembly.body: P-011 kerf, wet, glue, fill. H-019 4″ port. Clear oscillator stroke if fitted.

assembly.title: True drum on full-width sled
assembly.body: P-013 abrasive face-up on the ways. TIR ≤ 0.002″. Then H-022 Velcro + spiral paper.

assembly.title: Indicator clock A/B — parallel home
assembly.body: Paper on. |A−B| ≤ 0.003″. Lock home dog. Record the reading.

assembly.title: Test panel + pass schedule
assembly.body: 80 / 120 / 180. Caliper four corners. If scatter > 0.003″, re-clock. Finish at 0.001″.

calibration.title: Disconnect power
calibration.body: Unplug. Hood off. Paper off for TIR; paper on for A/B parallel.

calibration.title: Seat the table on the vertical ways
calibration.body: Raise/lower through full travel. Shoes stay wrapped. No bind, no yaw. Square on the wear face — no twist.

calibration.title: Drum TIR
calibration.body: Indicator on mid-span OD. Rotate by hand. If > 0.002″, re-true on P-013 before wrapping.

calibration.title: Wrap & re-clock
calibration.body: Velcro then spiral paper. Paper is not uniform — A/B will change. This is the measurement that matters.

calibration.title: A/B parallel
calibration.body: Same indicator height, drive then idler. Uncouple left Acme; 1/10 turn ≈ 0.1000″. Recouple. Set home dog.

calibration.title: Hold-down height
calibration.body: Feelers under each roller vs drum. 0.030″ below. Leading snipe → ease outfeed spring; trailing → ease infeed.

calibration.title: Witness board
calibration.body: 6″ × 16″ maple, 80 grit, one pass. Ridge at overlap = idler high/low. Caliper corners. Log in the Build app.

calibration.title: Taper mode (optional)
calibration.body: Uncouple left, drop idler a few thousandths, sand, then return to home dog — do not re-invent parallel each time.

name: WALTER DS-16 dedicated drum thickness sander
lineage: ShopNotes 86 → Ron Walters → Rev A solid table → Rev B geometry → Rev C precision axis

spec.bearing_drive: Mounted ball bearing, 1¼″ bore, self-aligning — FIXED
spec.bearing_idler: Mounted ball bearing, 1¼″ bore, self-aligning — FLOATING (axial)
spec.hood_method: Kerf-bent ¼″ pine/birch ply, sawdust-glue filled
modernizations: Dual ½-10 Acme table screws on the drum centerline, chain-coupled
Left screw uncouples for taper; dog stop returns to parallel home
Vertical captured UHMW ways — table is a lifting carriage, not a Y-slide
Housed stretchers (¼″ dados) + through-screws for racking stiffness
Stack-drill side panels as a pair; floating idler bearing (axial pad, not YZ slots)
Torsion-box table + phenolic / tooling-plate wear face
Spring hold-down rollers infeed + outfeed — kills snipe and chatter
Full-width truing sled; re-clock after paper wrap (ALN-01)
Dial-indicator pad on drive side; 0.001″ pass schedule
Optional ⅛″ slow oscillation (gear motor) to erase spiral tracks
Structural 6061 drum shell + turned plugs (Option B disc stack documented)
Tapered UHMW gib + ¼-28 idler jack for ALN-01
Frame housed dados through-bolted (H-034) — glue is not primary structure

notes: Keep 16.5″ (419 mm) clear between inner faces even if ply is 18 mm Euro BB instead of ¾″.
Way rebate 0.520″ / project 0.230″ so the 16″ table fits the span.
